nativeOutcome: One additional household not experiencing very low food security at 12 months
decision: Our revised conditional best guess is about $59.6 million per10 incremental QALYs for Community Markets, not the entire Food Bank. Table2's .023 food-insecure-versus-secure utility contrast replaces the old .008 mixed-population policy contrast; a separate50% funding-additionality judgment is now explicit. Other central inputs remain USD300 per26-week course,5% exit probability,35% reaching the study's secure category, one adult-equivalent,50% utility transfer and half an effective year. This is not a measured SFMFB effect or verified marginal offer. It is not a leading health-only use of donations under this model; food consumption and dignity benefits are outside the QALY comparison.

sourceEvidence.design: Longitudinal observational target-trial emulation using nationally representative Medical Expenditure Panel Survey data
sourceEvidence.population: Adults who screened positive for food insecurity; 1,368 were food insecure under the full survey module
sourceEvidence.contrast: Scenario2: hypothetical all-adult-food-insecure versus all-adult-food-secure states, not Scenario1's mixed status quo
sourceEvidence.boundary: Table2 Scenario2 estimates SF-6D .804 if all food insecure versus .827 if all food secure: .023 (95%CI .010–.036). This observational counterfactual state contrast is not a measured Community Market effect. Annual QALYs require the utility difference to last a year. Scenario1's .008 compares a mixed status quo with all secure; its prose conversion to80/100,000 is arithmetically inconsistent, though .827−.819 supports .008. We use Scenario2 for modeled individual state transitions, with an explicit transfer judgment.

modeledDonorCostPerHouseholdCourseUsd.basis: USD300 is a judgmental incremental operating allowance, oriented by legacy pantry expenses net of recognized donated food/services. That subtraction still contains depreciation and is not an exact cash flow or marginal Community Market quote. USD1,160 is a full recognized-accounting comparator, not a complete economic resource valuation.

causalExitFromVeryLowFoodSecurityProbabi.basis: The native model heavily discounts the 228-person Freshplace randomized result for differences in population, geography, service bundle, dose, and follow-up. SFMFB has not published a causal Community Market result; null or harm remains outside the finite positive range.

shareOfExitsReachingFullHouseholdFoodSec.basis: With no Community Market transition matrix, the 35% share reaching the study's food-secure category is an MFI judgment. The study dichotomizes USDA adult-module0–2 affirmative responses as secure (including marginal) and3+ as insecure. Exiting very low food security need not cross this threshold; it is not necessarily high food security.

adultEquivalentBeneficiariesPerHousehold.basis: The central model credits one adult-equivalent per household and excludes child and caregiver effects. The range reflects uncertainty about household composition and within-household benefit allocation; SFMFB publishes neither for the modeled cohort.

retainedShareOfObservedUtilityEffect.basis: Retain50% of the observational .023 state contrast for residual confounding and SF population/program transfer. This does not include donor funding displacement, which is modeled separately; adult allocation and duration have their own inputs.

effectiveDurationYears.basis: The midpoint allows for gradual onset during the 26-week course and limited persistence to the 12-month endpoint. The timing and persistence of a Community Market food-security change have not been measured.

modeledBridge.formula: causal_exit_probability * share_reaching_study_food_secure_state * adult_equivalent_beneficiaries * state_utility_difference * retained_share * effective_duration_years * funding_additionality
modeledBridge.nullBoundary: The numeric range is conditional on a positive Community Market effect, some modeled exits reaching full food security, a positive adult health-utility relationship, and donor additionality. SFMFB has not published a causal Community Market result or a current marginal funding plan; the health-utility anchor is observational. If the program has no causal effect, leaves every household food insecure, causes harm, produces only transient change outside the assumed duration, or a gift displaces public funding, commodities, or existing private support, the impact price has no finite positive upper bound.

fundingAdditionality.basis: Judgmental share of an additional funded course that expands service rather than replacing already funded operations. Separate from clinical transfer and the causal program effect. No current donor expansion offer verified.

evidenceWeaknesses.label: Food-security state transition
evidenceWeaknesses.why: The native model estimates exit from very low food security, while the utility study estimates eliminating adult food insecurity. The 35% full-food-security share is an explicit MFI judgment because no cohort transition matrix is published.

evidenceWeaknesses.label: Household-to-person allocation
evidenceWeaknesses.why: QALYs accrue to people, but the native outcome is per household. The central one-adult-equivalent allocation excludes children and is not an SFMFB measurement.

evidenceWeaknesses.label: Health-utility transfer
evidenceWeaknesses.why: Scenario2's .023 is an observational counterfactual food-state contrast, not a causal effect of this service. The50% retention is judgmental. Using the old .008 proxy with all current other inputs makes the price2.875 times higher.

evidenceWeaknesses.label: Timing and persistence
evidenceWeaknesses.why: A 12-month food-security endpoint does not reveal onset or area under the health-utility curve. The 0.5-year midpoint is a decision assumption.

evidenceWeaknesses.label: Program effect and marginal funding
evidenceWeaknesses.why: The 5% effect is transferred from a different bundled pantry model, and the $300 course cost is a judgmental operating allowance oriented by pantry accounts, not a cash-flow calculation. Neither is a measured marginal Community Market result or price.

excludedBenefits: Child health, development, school attendance, caregiver relief, and within-household spillovers
Diet quality, stress, mental health, medical spending, mortality, and benefits-enrollment gains not captured by the adult food-security utility transfer
Food value, participant time, volunteer time, donated services, public commodities, and other social-resource costs outside the donor-cash boundary
Benefits from neighborhood pantries, home delivery, CalFresh outreach, policy work, and other Food Bank programs
requiredEvidence: Report the full USDA food-security transition matrix for a defined Community Market cohort, including high, marginal, low, and very low categories.

Report unique household composition and collect preference-based health utility for adults and age-appropriate measures for children at baseline, intermediate time points, 12 months, and post-program follow-up.
Use randomization or a credible concurrent comparison with complete participant flow, exposure, missing-data analysis, and a pre-specified causal estimand.
Publish incremental program cost, public/private/commodity displacement, current capacity, and dated $100K, $1M, and $10M marginal plans.
